blocks.text: Dohra:

Now listen to the episode about the Malwa Singhs, The way Khalsa Panth took the initiative to help them. The way the Phulkian dynasty expanded their empire, They way they occupied more territories with a dash. (1)
lines: Now listen to the episode about the Malwa Singhs,
The way Khalsa Panth took the initiative to help them.
The way the Phulkian dynasty expanded their empire,
They way they occupied more territories with a dash.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The moment Khalsa Panth force went out of Malwa, Soon would the Mughals invade the Malwa region. Looting and plundering they would demand a large ransom, Which the Malwa people could never manage to pay. (2)
lines: The moment Khalsa Panth force went out of Malwa,
Soon would the Mughals invade the Malwa region.
Looting and plundering they would demand a large ransom,
Which the Malwa people could never manage to pay.

blocks.text: From the front would the Malerkotla Pathans lead the Mughals, All the Hindus they wished to evict from Malwa. Thereupon did the Malwa chiefs made a resolution, Must they invite the Khalsa Panth to destroy Maleri Pathans. (3)
lines: From the front would the Malerkotla Pathans lead the Mughals,
All the Hindus they wished to evict from Malwa.
Thereupon did the Malwa chiefs made a resolution,
Must they invite the Khalsa Panth to destroy Maleri Pathans.

blocks.text: Deciding thus, Ala Singh himself proceeded to invite the Khalsa, Taking Bhai Buddha Singh father of Gurbakhsh Singh1 with him. As Khalsa Panth force was stationed at Amritsar, Many a gift did Ala Singh arrange for the Panth. (4)
lines: Deciding thus,
Ala Singh himself proceeded to invite the Khalsa,
Taking Bhai Buddha Singh father of Gurbakhsh Singh1 with him.
As Khalsa Panth force was stationed at Amritsar,
Many a gift did Ala Singh arrange for the Panth.

blocks.text: As Khalsa Panth held a daily congregation at Akal Takht, The whole Khalsa Panth would attend the evening prayer. Thus accompanied by his brothers did Ala Singh, Stand before the Khalsa Panth with folded hands. (5)
lines: As Khalsa Panth held a daily congregation at Akal Takht,
The whole Khalsa Panth would attend the evening prayer.
Thus accompanied by his brothers did Ala Singh,
Stand before the Khalsa Panth with folded hands.

blocks.text: Dohra:
As Ala Singh narrated his tale of woe, Khalsa Panth lent their ears to his plea. He narrated the way the Mughals harassed him, And the way Malerkotla Pathans invaded them. (6)
lines: As Ala Singh narrated his tale of woe,
Khalsa Panth lent their ears to his plea.
He narrated the way the Mughals harassed him,
And the way Malerkotla Pathans invaded them.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Narrating how the Malerkotla Pathans harassed Malwa Singhs, He narrated how Malerkotla Pathans ransacked their land. Hearing this, the Khalsa Panth did respond, Definitely would the Khalsa Panth destroy the Pathans. (7)
lines: Narrating how the Malerkotla Pathans harassed Malwa Singhs,
He narrated how Malerkotla Pathans ransacked their land.
Hearing this, the Khalsa Panth did respond,
Definitely would the Khalsa Panth destroy the Pathans.

blocks.text: Must S. Ala Singh lay a trap for the Pathans, Must they be taken out of their fortified forts. That way would the Singhs beat the Pathans, Once the Pathans came within the Khalsa's range. (8)
lines: Must S.
Ala Singh lay a trap for the Pathans,
Must they be taken out of their fortified forts.
That way would the Singhs beat the Pathans,
Once the Pathans came within the Khalsa's range.

blocks.text: Same advice did Ala Singh accept, Same plan would he execute after reaching back. Surely would the Khalsa Panth join Ala Singh, Such a solemn vow did Khalsa make at Akal Takht. (9)
lines: Same advice did Ala Singh accept,
Same plan would he execute after reaching back.
Surely would the Khalsa Panth join Ala Singh,
Such a solemn vow did Khalsa make at Akal Takht.

blocks.text: Soon after celebrating Diwali (at Amritsar), Certainly would the Khalsa force proceed towards him. "Tikka Bhai Dooj2" day did they fix for the attack, S. Bhuddha Singh would lead them from the front. (10)
lines: Soon after celebrating Diwali (at Amritsar),
Certainly would the Khalsa force proceed towards him.
"Tikka Bhai Dooj2" day did they fix for the attack,
S.
Bhuddha Singh would lead them from the front.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Once again before departure from Amritsar, Did Ala Singh appeal to the Khalsa Panth: Definitely would the Mughals annihilate him, In case Khalsa Panth failed to turn up. (11)
lines: Once again before departure from Amritsar,
Did Ala Singh appeal to the Khalsa Panth: Definitely would the Mughals annihilate him,
In case Khalsa Panth failed to turn up.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, the Khalsa Panh reiterated their pledge, Surely would the Khalsa Panth force join him. Arriving back, same plan did Ala Singh execute, A formidable fort did he raise in Malerkotla region. (12)
lines: Thereupon, the Khalsa Panh reiterated their pledge,
Surely would the Khalsa Panth force join him.
Arriving back, same plan did Ala Singh execute,
A formidable fort did he raise in Malerkotla region.

blocks.text: Close to the village Sanghera near Barnala, A temporary makeshift shelter did he raise. Hearing this, did the Malerkotla Pathans invade, Raikot chiefs did they bring for plundering. (13)
lines: Close to the village Sanghera near Barnala,
A temporary makeshift shelter did he raise.
Hearing this, did the Malerkotla Pathans invade,
Raikot chiefs did they bring for plundering.

blocks.text: Equipped with artillery guns and small fire arms, Ala Singh's force did they surround from all sides. As they took positions after arriving there, Ala Singh looked forward to Khalsa's support. (14)
lines: Equipped with artillery guns and small fire arms,
Ala Singh's force did they surround from all sides.
As they took positions after arriving there,
Ala Singh looked forward to Khalsa's support.

blocks.text: From the other side the Khalsa Panth started, With the beat of war drums did they proceed. Being led by Bhai Buddha Singh from the front, Day and night they kept advancing after crossing the rivers. (15)
lines: From the other side the Khalsa Panth started,
With the beat of war drums did they proceed.
Being led by Bhai Buddha Singh from the front,
Day and night they kept advancing after crossing the rivers.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Whenever the Khalsa Panth force felt famished, An odd village would they ransack for provisions. As they heard the gunfire from Mughal positions, They put up a camp within the vicinity of Mughals. (16)
lines: Whenever the Khalsa Panth force felt famished,
An odd village would they ransack for provisions.
As they heard the gunfire from Mughal positions,
They put up a camp within the vicinity of Mughals.

blocks.text: Thereupon, did Buddha Singh advise the Khalsa Panth, They must not put up a camp in close vicinity. Lest the Mughals knowing about the Khalsa's arrival, They might then disperse and be gone from there. (17)
lines: Thereupon, did Buddha Singh advise the Khalsa Panth,
They must not put up a camp in close vicinity.
Lest the Mughals knowing about the Khalsa's arrival,
They might then disperse and be gone from there.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

So at night did the Khalsa force depart from there, They positioned themselves where Buddha Singh suggested. The daily dose of opium and cannabis did they take, Their horses did they harness for the attack. (18)
lines: So at night did the Khalsa force depart from there,
They positioned themselves where Buddha Singh suggested.
The daily dose of opium and cannabis did they take,
Their horses did they harness for the attack.

blocks.text: Now listen to the plight of besieged Ala Singh, As he kept worrying about his fate day and night. Really in a fix did Ala Singh feel himself, As he felt insecure in a makeshift shelter. (19)
lines: Now listen to the plight of besieged Ala Singh,
As he kept worrying about his fate day and night.
Really in a fix did Ala Singh feel himself,
As he felt insecure in a makeshift shelter.

blocks.text: As the Mughal Pathan forces advanced nearer, Many in Ala Singh's camp felt highly concerned. In case the Khalsa Panth force delayed their arrival, Surely would the Mughals destroy Ala Singh's camp. (20)
lines: As the Mughal Pathan forces advanced nearer,
Many in Ala Singh's camp felt highly concerned.
In case the Khalsa Panth force delayed their arrival,
Surely would the Mughals destroy Ala Singh's camp.

blocks.text: As they kept looking impatiently for the Khalsa force, No where did they hear the dust and din of their footfalls. They felt the Majhail Singhs were unconcerned with their fate, Even as the provisions also started depleting at that moment. (21)
lines: As they kept looking impatiently for the Khalsa force,
No where did they hear the dust and din of their footfalls.
They felt the Majhail Singhs were unconcerned with their fate,
Even as the provisions also started depleting at that moment.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Ala Singh being a man with lot of patience, Patience did he advise to his people. In high spirits must his people remain, Surely would the Khalsa Panth arrive soon. (22)
lines: Ala Singh being a man with lot of patience,
Patience did he advise to his people.
In high spirits must his people remain,
Surely would the Khalsa Panth arrive soon.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Khalsa Panth had reached quite near the Pathans, They observed their position as the sun arose. Thereafter, the Khalsa Panth attacked after a prayer, May God enable them to destroy their enemies. (23)
lines: Khalsa Panth had reached quite near the Pathans,
They observed their position as the sun arose.
Thereafter, the Khalsa Panth attacked after a prayer,
May God enable them to destroy their enemies.

blocks.text: The Khalsa emblems did the Singhs unfurl, Many a time did they beat their wardrums. Pulling at the reins of their war horses, With slogans of war did they launch an attack. (24)
lines: The Khalsa emblems did the Singhs unfurl,
Many a time did they beat their wardrums.
Pulling at the reins of their war horses,
With slogans of war did they launch an attack.

blocks.text: As the Khalsa force advanced with the beat of drums, A cloud of dust did the Mughals spot rising. Like thundering clouds did the war drums beat, Like a lightning did the Khalsa flags shine. (25)
lines: As the Khalsa force advanced with the beat of drums,
A cloud of dust did the Mughals spot rising.
Like thundering clouds did the war drums beat,
Like a lightning did the Khalsa flags shine.

blocks.text: Such an intense volley of fire did the Singhs make, As if a hailstorm was falling from the skies. With such speed did Mughal soldiers start falling, As sparks flew from fire and died down. (26)
lines: Such an intense volley of fire did the Singhs make,
As if a hailstorm was falling from the skies.
With such speed did Mughal soldiers start falling,
As sparks flew from fire and died down.

blocks.text: Dohra:
So suddenly did the Singhs pounce upon the Mughals, As a bird of prey pounces upon its victim. Like timid sparrows did the Mughals flee, As they had lost their nerve to keep up the fight. (27)
lines: So suddenly did the Singhs pounce upon the Mughals,
As a bird of prey pounces upon its victim.
Like timid sparrows did the Mughals flee,
As they had lost their nerve to keep up the fight.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Thereafter, the Khalsa force drew their swords, Each single Singh killed two of Mughal soldiers; No Mughal could stand to face the Khalsa attack, Everyone deserted for fear of getting killed. (28)
lines: Thereafter, the Khalsa force drew their swords,
Each single Singh killed two of Mughal soldiers;
No Mughal could stand to face the Khalsa attack,
Everyone deserted for fear of getting killed.

blocks.text: Whosoever was found carrying any weapon, Instantly was he killed by the Khalsa force. Whosoever surrendered after disarming himself, Khalsa Panth, being merciful, spared his life. (29)
lines: Whosoever was found carrying any weapon,
Instantly was he killed by the Khalsa force.
Whosoever surrendered after disarming himself,
Khalsa Panth, being merciful, spared his life.

blocks.text: From the other side Ala Singh attacked with his force, They killed all those-who advanced towards them. All their artillery guns and arms did Khalsa capture, The guns that they had positioned all around. (30)
lines: From the other side Ala Singh attacked with his force,
They killed all those-who advanced towards them.
All their artillery guns and arms did Khalsa capture,
The guns that they had positioned all around.

blocks.text: Highly delighted did Ala Singh feel, As all his cherished desires were fulfilled. Many a Pathan were put to death by Singhs, A horrible catastrophe did they pass through. (31)
lines: Highly delighted did Ala Singh feel,
As all his cherished desires were fulfilled.
Many a Pathan were put to death by Singhs,
A horrible catastrophe did they pass through.

blocks.text: Dohra:

After beating and plundering so many Mughal Pathans, Highly enriched and rewarded did the Khalsa feel. After beating the war drum of victory and triumph, At one place did the Khalsa Panth force assemble. (32)
lines: After beating and plundering so many Mughal Pathans,
Highly enriched and rewarded did the Khalsa feel.
After beating the war drum of victory and triumph,
At one place did the Khalsa Panth force assemble.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Now listen about Ala Singh's state of mind, The haste with which he went to the Khalsa Panth. From a distance he spotted the Khalsa emblems, From a distance he heard congregational sermons. (33)
lines: Now listen about Ala Singh's state of mind,
The haste with which he went to the Khalsa Panth.
From a distance he spotted the Khalsa emblems,
From a distance he heard congregational sermons.

blocks.text: With folded hands did Ala Singh bow down, Dismounting from a horse did he touch Khalsa's feet. With repeated bows did he keep saluting the Panth, With reverence did he touch the feet of Nihang Singhs. (34)
lines: With folded hands did Ala Singh bow down,
Dismounting from a horse did he touch Khalsa's feet.
With repeated bows did he keep saluting the Panth,
With reverence did he touch the feet of Nihang Singhs.

blocks.text: Handfuls of rupees did he offer to the Khalsa Panth, For conducting a thanks giving prayer did he plead. The veteran Singhs as had lost their horses in the fight, Instantly did he compensate them with new horses. (35)
lines: Handfuls of rupees did he offer to the Khalsa Panth,
For conducting a thanks giving prayer did he plead.
The veteran Singhs as had lost their horses in the fight,
Instantly did he compensate them with new horses.

blocks.text: To some Singhs he gave promissory notes with a prayer, Every passerby did he please on the way. As he arrived near the Khalsa Panth congregation, Reverentially did he remove his shoes from his feet. (36)
lines: To some Singhs he gave promissory notes with a prayer,
Every passerby did he please on the way.
As he arrived near the Khalsa Panth congregation,
Reverentially did he remove his shoes from his feet.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Bowing and saluting time and again, Did he arrive at the Khalsa congregation. Folding his hands did he bow down, Loudly did he utter the Khalsa greetings. (37)
lines: Bowing and saluting time and again,
Did he arrive at the Khalsa congregation.
Folding his hands did he bow down,
Loudly did he utter the Khalsa greetings.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
"Waheguru ji ki Fateh" did he speak aloud, With similar greetings did the Khalsa respond. For a few minutes was Ala Singh kept standing, As had been the tradition among the Khalsa Panth. (38)
lines: "Waheguru ji ki Fateh" did he speak aloud,
With similar greetings did the Khalsa respond.
For a few minutes was Ala Singh kept standing,
As had been the tradition among the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: The Khalsa Panth seal which Ala Singh had kept safely, With a prayer did he offer to Baba Deep Singh3 . Thereafter, Ala Singh ordered for a lavish community meal, Hundred and one offerings of sacred pudding did he make. (39)
lines: The Khalsa Panth seal which Ala Singh had kept safely,
With a prayer did he offer to Baba Deep Singh3 .
Thereafter,
Ala Singh ordered for a lavish community meal,
Hundred and one offerings of sacred pudding did he make.

blocks.text: Money for provisions did he hand over to Gurbakhsh Singh, Who himself would serve the food to congregation. Many a horse did he present as gifts to Singhs, At the base camp where Jassa Singh Ahluwalia camped. (40)
lines: Money for provisions did he hand over to Gurbakhsh Singh,
Who himself would serve the food to congregation.
Many a horse did he present as gifts to Singhs,
At the base camp where Jassa Singh Ahluwalia camped.

blocks.text: To those Singhs belonging to Sodhi and Bedi clans, Gifts of choicest horses did he make to them. S. Chain Singh, being one of the leading young Singhs, To him Ala Singh presented one of the choicest horses. (41)
lines: To those Singhs belonging to Sodhi and Bedi clans,
Gifts of choicest horses did he make to them.
S.
Chain Singh, being one of the leading young Singhs,
To him Ala Singh presented one of the choicest horses.

blocks.text: Dohra:

There used to be one Singh from the scheduled castes, S. Biru Singh4 was the name of this young Singh. A contingent of thirteen hundred mounted Singhs did he command, A separate emblem and war drum did he possess. (42)
lines: There used to be one Singh from the scheduled castes,
S.
Biru Singh4 was the name of this young Singh.
A contingent of thirteen hundred mounted Singhs did he command,
A separate emblem and war drum did he possess.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The first gift of a horse did Ala Singh give to him, To other Singhs he presented gifts thereafter. Those who lead from the front during a fight, They are the first to be honoured by the Khalsa Panth. (43)
lines: The first gift of a horse did Ala Singh give to him,
To other Singhs he presented gifts thereafter.
Those who lead from the front during a fight,
They are the first to be honoured by the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Once S. Biru Singh had (defected from the Khalsa Panth), With the Mughals' army had he enlisted himself. He having thirteen hundred mounted soldiers under his command, Instantly had the Mughals enlisted him in their army. (44)
lines: Once S.
Biru Singh had (defected from the Khalsa Panth),
With the Mughals' army had he enlisted himself.
He having thirteen hundred mounted soldiers under his command,
Instantly had the Mughals enlisted him in their army.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, the Mughals wrote a stinging letter to Khalsa Panth, Their great warrior had joined the Mughals as their menial. The person whom the Khalsa Panth considered a great warrior, That Islamic butcher would now fight on Mughal's behalf. (45)
lines: Thereafter, the Mughals wrote a stinging letter to Khalsa Panth,
Their great warrior had joined the Mughals as their menial.
The person whom the Khalsa Panth considered a great warrior,
That Islamic butcher would now fight on Mughal's behalf.

blocks.text: That Islamic butcher was now tending Mughals' cow herds, With the Khalsa Panth was he itching for a fight. Hearing this, the Khalsa Panth wrote a missive to him, Of breach of faith and trust did they accuse him. (46)
lines: That Islamic butcher was now tending Mughals' cow herds,
With the Khalsa Panth was he itching for a fight.
Hearing this, the Khalsa Panth wrote a missive to him,
Of breach of faith and trust did they accuse him.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The epistle that the Mughals had written to Khalsa Panth, As Islamic butcher had they described him in that letter. Must he stay with Mughals if he was an Islamic butcher, Must he return to the Khalsa fold if he was a Singh. (47)
lines: The epistle that the Mughals had written to Khalsa Panth,
As Islamic butcher had they described him in that letter.
Must he stay with Mughals if he was an Islamic butcher,
Must he return to the Khalsa fold if he was a Singh.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
In case he did not return to the Khalsa Panth fold, Condemned would he remain in both the worlds. Hearing this, instantly did he return to the Panth, As he held the KhalsaPanth in great esteem. (48)
lines: In case he did not return to the Khalsa Panth fold,
Condemned would he remain in both the worlds.
Hearing this, instantly did he return to the Panth,
As he held the KhalsaPanth in great esteem.

blocks.text: The gifts in liquid cash which he had brought, These also did he place before the Khalsa Panth. With him his whole community also joined the Khalsa, Their offerings they also made to the Khalsa Panth. (49)
lines: The gifts in liquid cash which he had brought,
These also did he place before the Khalsa Panth.
With him his whole community also joined the Khalsa,
Their offerings they also made to the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Thereafter, those who still remained defiant, They too were attacked by the Khalsa Panth. Many were killed while many others spared, Most of them had to submit to Khalsa's sovereignty. (50)
lines: Thereafter, those who still remained defiant,
They too were attacked by the Khalsa Panth.
Many were killed while many others spared,
Most of them had to submit to Khalsa's sovereignty.
